attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, asserted in his own voice.

semantics.note: Verbatim. The text right after it sets Ray-Ban hardware revenue apart, so treating hardware as separate is consistent with the claim.

contract.note: Reading 'money' as direct revenue fits the context, and Q1 2025 is a reasonable period. Requiring an identified accounting basis is strict, but it applies equally to support and contradiction.

evidence.note: TechCrunch reports, from a plaintiffs' filing, that Meta gets some Llama revenue share. No period or amount, and it is a litigation allegation, so it does not establish Q1 2025 revenue.

reviews.rationale: e1 casts doubt on the 'any money' claim but does not show direct generative-AI revenue recognised in Jan–Mar 2025. Nothing in the packet shows zero revenue either. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Shifting from Altman to OpenAI under Altman is reasonable. Dropping the rhetorical 'one skill' clause is appropriate.

contract.note: Defining 'functioning agent' as dependable, useful multistep completion (not flawless) is an ordinary reading. June 2025 as the period and leaving the undefined intelligence clause unscored are both fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure that Codex was available in June 2025. It shows the product existed, not that it completes tasks dependably.
January 2025 Operator launch post, with limitations the company admits itself. Not a June measurement.
April 2025 independent benchmark: Operator succeeded on 61% of tasks. Shows real function and frequent failure. Earlier than the target period.

reviews.rationale: Delivered agents existed (Codex, Operator), but the packet has no independent June 2025 measurement of dependable multistep performance. A 61% success rate from April neither clearly meets nor clearly fails 'functioning'. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Covers both commitments: a small paying share and weak adoption outside ChatGPT. The occasional-versus-daily-user remark is descriptive and fairly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'very few' as a small share and 'weren't there' as lacking substantial adoption is ordinary. 'Outside' has no defined scope, so the second part depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: The Verge, citing The Information on April 1, 2025: 20M paying subscribers. Together with the 500M user figure this backs the paying-share part only.
Secondary report dated April 1, 2025: about 4% of 500M weekly users pay. Supports 'very few' as a proportion.
Court allegation repeating OpenAI's website figure of 3M API developers, with no activity window and no comparable benchmark. Does not settle the 'outside ChatGPT' part.

reviews.rationale: The paying-share part is supported: about 4% of users paid in the quarter. The claim that adoption outside ChatGPT is lacking has no comparable measure; 3M developers neither confirms nor refutes it. The support condition requires both parts, so the claim as a whole is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. He cites the Salesforce study in support and endorses its finding.

semantics.note: Captures the causal link from LLM unreliability to agents being unworkable. The Apple reasoning clause is correctly left out of scope.

contract.note: Reading 'fucked as a concept' as fundamentally unable to do dependable multistep automation is ordinary. Counting safeguards as part of the agent system is reasonable. No reliability threshold is supplied.

evidence.note: Salesforce paper: performance drops on multi-turn tasks, which supports the reliability concern. The same paper reports over 83% on workflow execution, which weakens any claim of universal failure.
METR, March 2025: agents cannot reliably do long tasks but nearly always succeed on short ones and are improving. Supports current limits only, not an inherent barrier.
Developer-reported 2026 preprint showing high benchmark success from system architecture. Challenges impossibility, but has no independent replication.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows real reliability limits, but not that LLM unreliability makes agents fundamentally unworkable. The counterexamples are partial or vendor-reported. Neither condition is met.
